name: Dead Meridian

stars.name: Meridian
stars.notes: Hot, luminous A-type star with extreme UV output. Young and brilliant, it sterilizes everything within its considerable reach. No world in this system can support life.

planets.name: Flashpoint
planets.notes: Superheated volcanic world with surface magma lakes and a thin atmosphere of vaporized rock. Tidal interactions with the star drive constant geological upheaval.

planets.name: Cordon
planets.notes: Large, airless world whose surface has been baked to ceramic hardness by stellar radiation. Automated interdiction platforms orbit in a dense shell, enforcing the exclusion zone.

planets.name: Terminus
planets.notes: Cold, dark world at the system's outer edge. Its single moon shows evidence of artificial excavation—deep shafts bored into the subsurface that predate Terran discovery of the system.

planets.name: Pale Reach
planets.notes: Distant ice dwarf barely bound to the system. Its eccentric orbit takes it far from the star, making it useful as a navigation waypoint for patrols enforcing the interdiction zone.

anomalies.name: The Meridian Line
anomalies.location: Precise stellar meridian, extending from pole to pole of the star
anomalies.notes: A razor-thin plane of gravitational distortion aligned with the star's rotational axis. Objects crossing the plane experience brief but intense tidal forces. Origin unknown; the phenomenon predates system discovery.

anomalies.name: The Shafts
anomalies.notes: Precisely bored tunnels extending kilometers into the moon's crust, too regular to be natural. Interior surfaces are fused smooth. Whatever was extracted—or interred—has left no trace.

asteroid_belts.name: The Dead Zone
asteroid_belts.notes: Thin, radiation-blasted asteroid belt. Automated kill-sats positioned throughout enforce the interdiction zone by destroying any vessel that does not transmit proper authorization codes.

stations.name: Interdiction Buoy Network
stations.notes: Fully automated network of armed buoys that warn, then fire upon, any vessel entering the system without proper clearance. Maintained by quarterly service runs from neighboring systems.

stations.name: Research Platform Null
stations.notes: Small, heavily classified research station investigating the Meridian Line phenomenon and the artificial shafts on Terminus's moon. Crew rotates every 60 days under strict information quarantine.

faction_control.notes: Joint classified jurisdiction. The system is designated an interdiction zone—entry without authorization is met with lethal automated force. The official reason is stellar radiation hazard; the actual reason is the unexplained anomalies.

history: Discovered in 2531 during a stellar survey, Dead Meridian was initially cataloged as a sterile system of no strategic value until the survey ship detected the Meridian Line gravitational anomaly and the artificial excavations on Terminus's moon.

In 2548, a Terran research expedition entered the shafts on Terminus's moon and lost contact for 72 hours. When recovered, three of the seven team members were dead and the survivors could not coherently describe what they had encountered. The system was immediately classified and interdicted.

Since 2548, Research Platform Null has conducted ongoing investigation under extreme security protocols. All findings are classified at the highest level. Three unauthorized vessels have been destroyed by the interdiction buoy network, their identities and purposes never publicly disclosed.
description: Dead Meridian is a system of blinding light and deep secrets. Its blue-white A-type star blazes with enough ultraviolet radiation to sterilize any unshielded surface within the system, and the four worlds that orbit it are accordingly dead—volcanic, barren, rocky, and frozen, in that order. The system should be utterly unremarkable, just another sterile collection of rocks around a hot star in the Scorch Expanse. It is not. The Meridian Line, a razor-thin plane of gravitational distortion aligned with the star's axis, has no known natural explanation. The precisely bored shafts on the moon of Terminus were made by something, and whatever made them is long gone but left questions that Terran science cannot yet answer.

The military's interest in Dead Meridian is not strategic in the conventional sense. There is nothing here to defend or supply. Instead, the system is interdicted because what it contains is potentially more dangerous than any weapon: evidence of a technology that predates human spaceflight by an unknown margin. The shafts are too precise to be natural, and the Meridian Line phenomenon does not correspond to any known physics. Research Platform Null's 85-person crew works under information quarantine so strict that they cannot communicate with family during their 60-day rotations. Whatever they are finding, it is being kept from everyone outside a very small circle.

The loss of three researchers in the 2548 expedition remains the system's most disturbing legacy. The surviving four were medically discharged and have never spoken publicly about what happened in the shafts. Their classified debriefings reportedly run to thousands of pages. Unofficial accounts suggest they encountered something that was not an artifact of the tunnels' creators but something that had moved in after—something that had been waiting. Whether this is credible intelligence or trauma-induced confabulation is a question that Research Platform Null is, presumably, still trying to answer.
